name: Sects and the War of Princes (Dark Ages, ST-Only)

text.content:
While feudalism dominates the Dark Medieval night, not all vampires rally under banners and crowns. Cainite society has always had its blood families and cults who gather vampires secretly in the shadows of princely thrones. Storytellers should use this material to seed hooks and NPCs rather than hand it directly to player characters as common knowledge - most of these groups are rumor and legend even within Cainite society.

The Inconnu

Many old, powerful Cainites of Rome simply vanished after its fall, apparently never heard from again. Rumor has it that these vampires lair beneath the cities, watching their younger brethren - some attempt to guide them from afar into avoiding their mistakes, while others are vengeful and wish only for all to suffer as they did in Rome. Some believe the sect was responsible in part for the fall of Constantinople; if so, the sect has changed its tactics recently, deciding only to watch and not interfere. The Inconnu are also believed to be leading the preservation of old, precious manuscripts as the War of Princes rages. Most princes publicly discount the Inconnu as Cainite folk legend - behind closed doors, they are less boastful.

The Order of Bitter Ashes

Cainites of this order seek the redemption of God that Caine rejected so long ago. No one quite knows when the order began, but it has spread through Europe and the Middle East. The knights believe it is their duty - a mandate from Christ Himself - to find and protect relics from falling into the wrong hands, be they Cainite or mortal. Some claim the knights ride ghoul stallions and battle the infernal; others say they have drunk Christ's blood and been freed from the Beast. Time has not been kind to the order, and its power is waning; much of its holdings are in ruins due to the Crusades, the Albigensian Crusade, the Reconquista and Cainite squabbles. Its headquarters in Scotland stands fast, but who knows how long it will last. Many knights are being baited by princes into fighting their wars, lured by promises of relics, yet the Ashen knights hold fast to their mandate and continue to search for and protect those worthy of God's redemption.

The Furores

Wherever there are powerful people, there are malcontents and outlaws. The Furores are considered rebels and bandits, refusing to bow to the Traditions of Caine and the rule of the elders - unlife should be a gift, not a shackle of eternal servitude, they say. Furores comprise vampires of both Low and High Clans unafraid to get their hands dirty carving out kingdoms amid artisans, performers and laborers in the growing cities and middle class. Still, as outlaws under Cainite rule, the Furores often face a nightly struggle to survive, whether in colonies outside the cities or using the guilds to hide their movements.

The Prometheans

This sect remembers and longs to re-create Carthage as it was before it fell into infamy. Naming themselves for the god who brought fire to humanity, these vampires want to enlighten both Cainites and kine in a "new Carthage." The sect has adherents from the High and Low Clans, who hope that targeting the lower classes and the new middle class will bring better results than trying to change the minds of elders. Prometheans have influence over the criminal elements of the cities as well as merchants and guilds.

The Cainite Heresy

The Heresy is one of the worst stains upon the Dark Medieval. A strange brew of Gnosticism, early Christian thought, Cainite belief and outright lies, the Heresy has used blasphemous teachings, coercion and evangelism to spread across the Church and Europe. The cult's most influential priests, the Crimson Curia, lead the Heresy by setting doctrine and attempting to coordinate its movements. The Curia maintains that God's mark upon Caine shows he was God's favorite, and that since Caine was touched by God, his descendants should be treated as prophets and angels. The Heresy has infiltrated the Catholic priesthood and even influenced the Road of Heaven, sending would-be pious Cainites into a spiral of further damnation. The involvement of the Heresy's Archbishop Nanses in the Fourth Crusade has convinced princes and ashen priests alike that the Heresy must be destroyed - though not all move against it for benevolent reasons, since many are simply envious of its wealth and power. The Fourth Crusade has divided the Crimson Curia, and the sect currently suffers internal strife.

pages.name: The War of Princes: Fields of Battle

text.content:
The fragile peace of the Long Night has crumbled, and Cainites rally around the banners of their lords and princes, vying for power or settling long-held grudges. This "war" began as a conflict between a number of very powerful, very active Methuselahs; the princes who control discrete domains are the most valuable pawns, since they may swear fealty to others but their domains can still be usurped through force of arms, treachery, or even from within if a prince can be persuaded to switch sides.

The staying (diablerie) of Saulot by Tremere is widely pointed to as having had the greatest impact on triggering the current conflict - almost overnight the Cainites changed forever, and even the Antediluvians are said to have shuddered in their sleep. The rise of the Tremere was soon followed by the rising of several Methuselahs from torpor, stirred by mortal events: Ventrue Methuselah Mithras awoke following the Norman Conquest of 1066; when the First Crusade took Jerusalem in 1096, Caliph Jamal of the Assamites called on his clan to push back the European vampires who came with the crusaders; Montano exerted influence over his Christian clanmates in Iberia to expel the Moorish vampires from the peninsula, beginning a "Shadow Reconquista"; High Lord Hardestadt of Germany moved east into Tzimisce lands to acquire domains for the Holy Roman Empire; and French Toreador withdrew support from the Ventrue prince of Paris. The sack of Constantinople during the Fourth Crusade (the "Bitter Crusade") - including the loss of Toreador Methuselah Michael the Archangel - proved the final spark that set the War of Princes ablaze: if a vampire wanted to survive the coming times, he needed to cement his power and move against his enemies before they could move against him.

The following are the most active fronts a Storyteller can use to frame chronicle-level conflict:

  • The Crusades - Each new crusade draws more Cainites into its grasp. The Fourth Crusade marched on Constantinople, the Fifth travels to Damietta (Egypt), and the Sixth goes to Jerusalem; in Europe, the Albigensian Crusade hunts the Cathars in France, and the Livonian Crusade sends German knights into Prussia and the Baltic to battle the pagans of the East. Some Cainites ride the wave of whatever a crusade brings, others use the battles to claim domain and hunt enemies (inviting retaliation), and the rest must deal with armies marching across their domains and shifting borders.
  • The Eastern Marches (the Omen War) - Ever since mortal magi used Tzimisce blood to create Clan Tremere, the Cainites of Eastern Europe have made it their mission to wipe out the usurpers. Two hundred years of fighting has only deepened hatreds on both sides; the Tremere seek out allies, using the Fiends' traditional isolation against them, and many princes are willing to offer covert support in exchange for a little blood magic. Ventrue of Germany and Hungary see the Omen War as a chance to make inroads into traditional Tzimisce territory in Prussia and Livonia.
  • The Inquisition and the Cainite Heresy - In 1230 what will become the Inquisition has not yet fully appeared, but Cainites are already reporting shadow operatives - monks, laity and knights of holy orders armed with faith and unusual powers - who seem to be its foot soldiers. Meanwhile the Cainite Heresy worries about the Church's hunt for heretics even as it works to further infiltrate it.
  • The Shadow Reconquista - Al-Andalus, the last Muslim stronghold in Europe, stands against the combined might of Aragon, Castile-Leon, Navarre and Portugal. Cordoba and Seville suffer the brunt of attacks while Granada braces for its turn. The mortal Reconquista is tearing the Lasombra apart, as Moorish and Christian Lasombra fall into an undeclared civil war over which side to support.
  • The Low Clans - Ignored and spat on, the Low Clans are beginning to plan their move against the arrogant High Clans. While princes look elsewhere, preoccupied with the War of Princes, members of the Low Clans grow their own power as bandit kings and guildmasters. Many are members of the Prometheans and Furores, and whisper of a great revolt apparently in the making against the High Clans.

Storyteller note: the term "vampire army" is misleading in play - the largest vampiric force on any given battlefield rarely holds more than a few dozen Cainites, though thralls, ghouls and mortal cat's-paws swell their ranks into something resembling a true army. For every prince who leads troops in the field, five more host ambassadors at their courts and make new alliances every night; use this ratio to keep chronicle-scale warfare from overwhelming the personal, political nature of most Cainite conflict.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter One: Introduction and Setting
